strings.name: Ang Lee
strings.role: Film director · Cross-cultural stories and image technology
strings.country: Taiwan (long active in the United States)
strings.summary: Ang Lee grew up and studied the arts in Taiwan before training in theatre and film in the United States. His early features, including The Wedding Banquet and Eat Drink Man Woman, explore tradition and intimate relationships. He later worked across languages and genres in Sense and Sensibility and Brokeback Mountain. Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon and Life of Pi expanded cross-cultural cinema’s reach, while his 3D and high-frame-rate films experiment with how audiences see images.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to the February 2025 DGA honor. A 2026 institutional event announcement was checked for recent context, without treating the announced event as completed; later film projects are not presented as finished.
strings.influence.rationale: Crossed languages and genres with Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Brokeback Mountain and Life of Pi, advancing intercultural exchange in cinema.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BFA, University of Illinois; MFA in film production, New York University, 1984
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Connecting cultural experiences through genre
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: From family comedy and martial arts to a Western love story, explores tensions between social expectations and private feeling.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Developing narrative and image technology
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Explored 3D, digital imagery and high-frame-rate photography in Life of Pi and Billy Lynn’s Long Halftime Walk.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Receives the DGA Lifetime Achievement Award
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Received the lifetime-achievement honor at the 77th Directors Guild of America Awards for his sustained work across genres.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Directs Gemini Man
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Used a digital character and high-frame-rate 3D imagery in an action film, continuing experiments beyond conventional cinema presentation.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Releases Billy Lynn’s Long Halftime Walk
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Shot an Iraq War-related story in 120 frames per second, 4K and 3D, exploring detail and immediacy in performance.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Wins another directing Oscar for Life of Pi
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Won his second directing Oscar for the 2012 film, which uses digital imagery in a tale of survival at sea.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Lust, Caution wins Venice’s Golden Lion
strings.timeline.event-05.text: The wartime story of emotion, identity and espionage won the festival’s top prize, examining private desire amid history.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Wins the directing Oscar for Brokeback Mountain
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Received his first directing Oscar for the 2005 love story, extending his examination of repressed emotions.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Directs Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Worked with the cast and an international production team to combine martial arts, love and social constraints for a wide audience.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Directs Sense and Sensibility
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Adapted Jane Austen in English, entering a new production setting while continuing themes of family and feeling in a British period drama.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Releases Eat Drink Man Woman
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Centered a Taipei family’s meals and generational relationships, weaving food, personal choices and traditional expectations together.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: The Wedding Banquet wins the Golden Bear
strings.timeline.event-10.text: The comedy about a cross-cultural family and a same-sex relationship shared Berlin’s Golden Bear, expanding his international profile.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Releases his first feature Pushing Hands
strings.timeline.event-11.text: After living and writing in New York, directed a feature about an immigrant family, generations and cultural adjustment.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Completes his film MFA at NYU
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Completed film-production training and the thesis film Fine Line, having previously studied theatre at the University of Illinois.
strings.timeline.event-13.title: Born in Pingtung, Taiwan
strings.timeline.event-13.text: Grew up in Taiwan, later attending arts school and developing an interest in directing from his experience with performance.
